title: Turn back, or God will sharpen his sword against you
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the wicked who refuse to turn back
note: Conditional warning addressed to hearers ('if you do not return'): an implicit call to repent, like recorded warnings at 49:22 and 74:5.

title: God appointed humankind to rule over the works of his hands
speaker: David (the psalmist), recalling God's appointment
topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
note: Recalls the Genesis 1:28 dominion over sheep, cattle, birds and fish; link as Additional Scripture (quoted in Hebrews 2:6–8).

title: Advisers urge the psalmist to flee to the mountains like a bird
speaker: unnamed advisers
note: Quoted counsel the psalmist rejects as faithless; the catalogue records such advice (cf. Job's wife, ot-job-v2-9e).

title: Whoever loves injustice hates his own soul
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: maxim that the Lord tests righteous and ungodly and loves righteous deeds; uncovered.

title: The fool says in his heart that there is no God
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Repeated as Greek Psalm 52:2–4: link that as Additional Scripture. 13:3 is quoted in Romans 3:10–18 (A121 is Study Context only).

title: Jacob and Israel are called to rejoice when God restores them
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Jussive call to rejoice, like recorded Greek Psalm 149:2. Same verse at Greek Psalm 52:7 (there indicative): link as Additional Scripture.

title: Whoever dwells with the Lord walks blamelessly and keeps his word
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Entrance liturgy: blameless walk, truthful speech, no harm or reproach to neighbours, honouring God-fearers, keeping oaths.

title: Do not lend at interest or take bribes against the innocent
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Echoes Torah laws C0206 (interest) and C0225 (bribes); closes 'whoever does these things will never be shaken'.

title: The Lord's law gives wisdom; in keeping it is great reward
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Praise of the law that teaches its worth, like recorded law-wisdom AUD-21-118-9; 18:12 'in keeping them there is great recompense'.

title: Only the clean-handed and pure in heart may ascend God's mountain
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Entrance liturgy like Greek Psalm 14: innocent hands, pure heart, no vain or deceitful oath.

title: The Lord teaches his way to the humble and God-fearing
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Context verse 24:8 and unflagged 24:9–10,12–14: declarative wisdom inside the prayer, uncovered.

title: Blessed is the forgiven one in whose mouth is no deceit
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Beatitude quoted in Romans 4:7–8 (no record there either); 31:5 testimony of confession supports it.

title: The warning against being as unthinking as a mule
speaker: the psalmist (or God) as teacher
note: Extend from 31:9 to 31:8–9: 'I will instruct you in the way you will go' introduces the same counsel.

title: The sinner has many scourges; mercy surrounds those who trust the Lord
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: wisdom saying between recorded 31:9 and 31:11, uncovered.

title: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord
speaker: the psalmist
note: Beatitude; declarative rather than directive.

title: Armies do not save kings; the Lord guards those who fear him
speaker: the psalmist
note: Candidate 32:19 completes unflagged 32:16–18: strength and horses do not save; the Lord rescues those who hope in him.

title: Approach the Lord and be enlightened; you will not be ashamed
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the meek who hear the psalm
note: Plural imperative to hearers between recorded 33:4 and 33:9–10.

title: Taste God's kindness and put your hope in him
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the meek who hear the psalm
note: Outside candidate list: extend from 33:9–10 to 33:8–11: the angel encamping (33:8) and 'seekers lack no good thing' (33:11) frame it.

title: The Lord's eyes are on the righteous; he is near the brokenhearted
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: motive of recorded 33:14–15; 33:16–17 quoted in 1 Peter 3:12 (A118), psalm verses unlinked.

title: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the Lord rescues them
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Closing wisdom of the acrostic psalm, incl. candidate 33:22 ('the death of sinners is evil'); its counsels 33:9–15 are recorded.

title: The wicked plots evil and has no fear of God before him
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Wisdom portrait of the wicked (35:2 quoted in Romans 3:18); descriptive, so low.

title: Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will grant your heart's requests
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
note: Imperative between recorded 36:3 and 36:5; only this verse of the run is missing.

title: The wicked will soon vanish, but the meek will inherit the land
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the faithful tempted to envy the wicked
note: Wisdom sayings motivating 36:7–8; 36:11 is echoed in Matthew 5:5 (AUD-44-5-3).

title: Better a little for the righteous than the great wealth of sinners
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Classic 'better than' wisdom saying; no record (nor for similar Proverbs 15:16, 16:8).

title: The sinner borrows and does not repay; the righteous gives freely
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: a clear uncovered wisdom saying in the same psalm (no signal detected).

title: The righteous is never forsaken; he shows mercy and lends all day
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: elder's testimony teaching mercy and lending, as in recorded AUD-21-111-1; uncovered.

title: Turn from evil and do good
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Extend from 36:27 to 36:27–29: 'For the Lord loves judgment… the righteous will dwell for ever' completes '…and dwell for age upon age'.

title: The righteous speaks wisdom and keeps God's law in his heart
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Portrait of righteous speech and an inward law, distinct from neighbouring records.

title: The Lord will not abandon the righteous to those seeking his life
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Declarative assurance leading into recorded 36:34 ('Wait for the Lord').

title: A call to watch the path of the upright and peaceful
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Extend from 36:37 to 36:37–40: the contrast (lawless destroyed) and 'salvation of the righteous is from the Lord' complete it.

title: Every person is a passing shadow, hoarding wealth for unknown heirs
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
note: Context verse 38:6 and unflagged 38:7: reflection on vanity inside a prayer, so low.

title: Blessed is the one who hopes in the Lord, not in vanities
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Beatitude directing trust and turning from vanities.

title: God desires a listening, obedient heart rather than sacrifice
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Same teaching as AUD-09-15-22 and ot-hosea-v6-6; quoted in Hebrews 10:5–7 (A103 is Study Context only).

title: Blessed is the one who considers the poor and needy
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Beatitude commending care for the poor, with the Lord's promised protection (40:3–4).

title: The royal song calls the king to reign for truth and justice
speaker: the sons of Korah (royal wedding song)
note: Extend from 44:5 to 44:4–5: 'Gird your sword… and stretch forth, prosper and reign' is one sentence.

title: God anoints the righteous king with the oil of gladness
speaker: the sons of Korah (royal wedding song)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported anointing to kingship (quoted of the Son in Hebrews 1:8–9, no record there); poetic, so low.

title: Mount Zion and Judah's daughters are called to rejoice in God's judgments
speaker: the sons of Korah
recipient: Mount Zion / the daughters of Judea
note: Jussive call to rejoice spoken within an address to God; opens the processional commands recorded at 47:13–14.

title: Wealth cannot ransom a life; rich and foolish alike die
speaker: the sons of Korah (wisdom psalm)
note: Core teaching of the wisdom psalm whose call to listen (48:2) and counsel (48:17) are recorded.

title: Do not be afraid when others grow rich
speaker: the sons of Korah (wisdom psalm)
note: Extend from 48:17 to 48:17–21: the 'for when he dies he takes nothing' reasons and refrain complete the counsel.

title: God calls his people to hear his testimony against them
speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
note: God's own summons 'Hear, My people… I testify unto you', like recorded 80:9.

title: God rebukes those who recite his covenant but hate his instruction
speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
note: Indictment naming hypocrisy, joining thieves and adulterers, deceit and slandering a brother; precedes recorded 49:22.

title: A warning to those who forget God
speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
note: Outside candidate list: 49:23 ('a sacrifice of praise will glorify Me') concludes God's speech and is uncovered; cf. 49:14.

title: A broken and humbled heart is the sacrifice God will not despise
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Context verse 50:19 with 50:18, not flagged: declarative teaching like recorded AUD-09-15-22 and ot-hosea-v6-6.

title: See the one who trusted wealth instead of making God his helper
speaker: the righteous, quoted by David
note: Lesson drawn from the boaster's downfall; compare recorded 61:11 (do not hope in wealth).

title: A rebuke to rulers who neither speak nor judge righteously
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: the sons of men who judge (rulers and judges)
note: Rebuke addressed to people, like recorded AUD-21-4-3 ('Sons of men, how long…'); implicit charge to judge uprightly.

title: Surely there is reward for the righteous and a God who judges
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: concluding wisdom of the psalm whose rebuke (57:2–3) is proposed above.

title: Do not place your trust in mortal rulers
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: God, in the hearing of the people
note: 'Human salvation is vain' (reason clause of a petition) restates recorded 145:3; repeated at Greek Psalm 107:13.

title: Submit to God, my soul, for my hope comes from him
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Self-exhortation (refrain of 61:2–3) like recorded AUD-21-41-6; leads into recorded 61:9.

title: Power belongs to God, who repays each according to his works
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: closes the counsel of recorded 61:9–11; quoted in Romans 2:6 (only broad AUD-49-2-1).

title: God's mercy is better than life itself
speaker: David (the psalmist)
recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
note: 'Better than' saying spoken to God in praise, so low (cf. 83:11).

title: The righteous will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Closing declarative assurance about the righteous; not a direct call, so low.

title: A song calling all the earth to praise God
speaker: the psalmist
note: Extend from 65:1–2 to 65:1–4: 'Say to God, How fearsome are Thy works…' continues the same call to all the earth.

title: God will not hear one who cherishes injustice in his heart
speaker: the psalmist
note: Teaching within the testimony invited at recorded 65:16; compare Proverbs 28:9.

title: All peoples are called to thank God and to fear him
speaker: the psalmist (community song)
note: Jussives partly addressed to God (cf. Study Context 34:27), but 66:8 matches recorded 32:8 ('Let all the earth fear the Lord').

title: A call to bless God in the assemblies of Israel
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: Outside candidate list: plural imperative 'In assemblies bless God' missed by the detector; uncovered call to worship.

title: Praise in song pleases God more than a sacrificial bull
speaker: David (the psalmist)
note: First-person vow carrying a teaching on praise over sacrifice; leads into recorded 68:33.

title: The psalmist's enemies urge one another to pursue and seize him
speaker: the psalmist's enemies
note: Quoted hostile exhortation; the catalogue records such plots elsewhere (ot-jeremiah-v11-19, ot-genesis-v37-20).

title: The wicked's prosperity ends in ruin; nearness to God is good
speaker: Asaph
recipient: God, in the hearing of readers
note: Candidate 72:18 sits in the wisdom psalm's resolution; 72:27–28 (unflagged) state its lesson.

title: Israel's enemies resolve to burn all God's feasts from the earth
speaker: Israel's enemies (quoted by Asaph)
note: 'Come, let us burn…' plot like recorded ot-jeremiah-v18-18 and ot-genesis-v37-20.

title: A warning against defiance and unjust speech
speaker: Asaph (God's words quoted)
note: Outside candidate list: extend from 74:6 to 74:6–9: 'for God is judge; He humbles one and raises another' grounds the warning.

title: If only my people would listen and walk in my ways
speaker: God (in Asaph's psalm)
note: Outside candidate list: Greek Psalm 80 has no passage in this batch; continues God's recorded appeals at 80:9–11.

title: The nations allied against Israel plot to wipe out its name
speaker: the coalition of nations and their rulers (quoted by Asaph)
note: 'Come, let us destroy them' (82:5) and 'Let us inherit God's sanctuary' (82:13, P01534); plots are recorded elsewhere (ot-jeremiah-v18-18).

title: Blessed are those dwelling in God's house, strengthened by him
speaker: the sons of Korah
recipient: God, in the hearing of worshippers
note: Beatitudes spoken to God, so low; they commend dwelling in God's house and pilgrim devotion.

title: One day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere
speaker: the sons of Korah
note: 'Better than' saying, God withholds no good from those who walk in innocence (83:12), and beatitude for those who hope in him.

title: Blessed are the people who know the festal shout
speaker: Ethan (the psalmist)
recipient: God, in the hearing of worshippers
note: Beatitude spoken to God, so low.

title: The Lord tells Samuel to anoint David
speaker: God (quoted by the psalmist)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: God's own account 'I found David My servant; with My holy oil I anointed him'.

title: David's sons must keep God's law or be punished with the rod
speaker: God (quoted by the psalmist)
note: Covenant condition of the Davidic covenant (cf. 2 Samuel 7:14, also unrecorded): keep my law; discipline, yet unbroken mercy.

title: God calls the sons of men to return
speaker: God (quoted in Moses' prayer)
note: Quoted divine word 'Return, sons of men'; may be a decree of mortality (return to dust) rather than a call to repent.

title: It is good to give thanks to the Lord morning and night
speaker: the psalmist (Sabbath song)
note: Declarative teaching on thanksgiving morning and night with instruments; compare recorded 146:1.

title: The senseless do not see that the wicked flourish only to perish
speaker: the psalmist (Sabbath song)
note: Context verse 91:7 with 91:8, not flagged: wisdom saying on the brief flourishing of the wicked.

title: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree in the Lord's house
speaker: the psalmist (Sabbath song)
note: Outside candidate list (no signal detected): wisdom portrait like recorded Psalm 1 (AUD-21-1-1).

summary: Most candidates are petitions or laments addressed to God (out of scope); the gaps are chiefly uncovered wisdom sayings and beatitudes (Greek Psalms 14, 23, 31, 33, 36, 40, 48, 91), God's quoted speech (49, 80, 88), a few calls to worship and quoted plots, with 14 adjacent misses outside the candidate list flagged in notes.
